proof_attempt_summary: Five D-0.5 proposal reviews refined the joint PN-PS-PNS prevalence-tube kernel, corrected and rechecked the binary response-type coupling, and compared inspected primary sources. The final reviewer reported field-tier novelty and no soundness or structure defects, but declined advancement solely because the final Kuroki-Cai (2011) theorem text was inaccessible; its public author manuscript was attested equation by equation and no matching joint theorem was found there. No Stage 0 derivation or Lean proof was attempted. The final-text overlap question remains open, and the operator's one-round cap ended this run.
tldr: Which PN–PS–PNS triples can coexist under outcome-only case–control sampling, sufficient finite adjustment, nonmonotone response, and a certified prevalence range? The proposed sharp answer is a generally nonconvex prevalence union of shared-response-type polygon fibers with an exact membership oracle. One positive rational table puts a triple inside all three marginal intervals yet outside the joint set and reconstructs a compatible triple exactly; support certificates and conservative simultaneous coverage support use of the geometry.
gap: The inspected public Kuroki–Cai manuscript supplies separate scalar PN/PNS formulas, while the inspected Sui theorem concerns PN alone. No inspected public theorem gives exact membership or nonconvexity for a retrospective prevalence-indexed PN–PS–PNS tube under one shared nonmonotone response law. The final Kuroki–Cai journal text is covered by the source-access caveat in related work.
